question.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $-1<2x-3\le 1$ and $3x>9.$
question.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

- First, we solve $-1<2x-3\le 1\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & <2x-3\le 1 \\ -1+3 & <2x-3+3\le 1+3 \\ 2 & <2x\le 4 \\ \frac{2}{2} & <\frac{2x}{2}\le \frac{4}{2} \\ 1 & <x\le 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/7f940af7e7480f83d89f47b53ec1f9b9d9d23e93d8419464055ada7b77c22be1.png)

- Then, we solve  $3x>9\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & >9 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & >\frac{9}{3} \\ x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/0883c587c9c164cc35fdf17b07f0d0bd3767c715c8c537e3c1013239194f22bc.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/5d31a9ebff15e2eb52faf5e3768576cf2de60205882fc130efb57f77ffad0b96.png)

$$

$$

It turns out that the solutions do not overlap at all. Therefore, there are no values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities simultaneously. So, there is no solution.
